prompt:
Iteration 7/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units

Plausible alternatives are additivity with zero interaction, saturation with attenuation, or a null interaction; all remain dataset-internal associations, not causal epistasis. Fifth, I register a demographic sex contrast to complete basic biological/technical stratification. Male versus female is registered as a weaker-dependency claim, but the primary purpose is to test whether any large, easily confounded population difference exists in the supplied dataset. A null result would strengthen the interpretation that the observed genetic/phenotypic predictors are not simply capturing broad demographic structure. Iteration 7/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

This exceeds the threshold and is in the accepted PTEN-loss stronger-dependency direction, so I accept it, but keep it active because it is a highly selected conditional stratum, exposed cell n=90, and PTEN has been the main boundary predictor across many comparisons; I therefore request independent validation. H102 is the only new central-predictor interaction that is promising: TP53-loss-by-KEAP1-loss interaction is +0.210 [0.019,0.400]. The point estimate exceeds the threshold and the interval excludes the null, but the lower bound is far below the effect-size threshold. This is scientifically suggestive that TP53-loss weaker dependency is not identical across KEAP1-loss backgrounds, but it is not decisive and remains unresolved and active. The other central interactions are essentially null or nonmeaningful in their claimed directions: TP53-by-SMARCA4 -0.032, KEAP1-by-SMARCA4 +0.023, TP53-by-lineage -0.033, and KEAP1-by-lineage -0.063. These support descriptive additivity of the main SMARCA4, TP53, and KEAP1 effects relative to SMARCA4 status or lineage subtype, rather than large claimed interactions. The PTEN interaction tests do not support strong effect modification as registered: PTEN-by-SMARCA4 and PTEN-by-TP53 are negative relative to their claimed directions and wide; PTEN-by-KEAP1 is +0.145, just below the threshold and wide; PTEN-by-lineage after excluding MSI-high is -0.008, essentially null. Thus the accepted PTEN-loss stronger-dependency evidence appears to be concentrated in clean conditional contexts, not established as a homogeneous global or interaction-modified pattern. Media 10% versus 2% serum is +0.012, and male versus female is -0.074; neither is meaningful at the 0.15 threshold, so the dataset does not show a large global culture-serum or sex confounding gradient in the dependency composite. I request validation only for H104 because it is the strongest newly accepted conditional PTEN result and independent confirmation would materially strengthen the PTEN boundary map. Iteration 7/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using

Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,

and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

H79 is decisive at its validation deadline: MSI-high versus non-MSI-high has discovery signed estimate +0.792 [0.676,0.907] and independent validation +0.826 [0.635,1.017]. Both intervals are entirely above the threshold and in the claimed stronger-dependency direction, so I accept and close MSI-high as a robust dataset-internal association with stronger composite dependency. H104 asks about PTEN loss in a very selected clean context: adenocarcinoma, MSI-nonhigh, and SMARCA4/TP53/KEAP1 intact. Discovery was +0.279 [0.186,0.373], which clears the threshold; independent validation is +0.203 [0.073,0.333]. The validation point estimate remains above threshold and the direction is consistent, but its lower bound falls below the threshold, likely because the selected exposed cell is small and the validation interval is conservative. I therefore maintain acceptance of H104 as a discovery-supported conditional association in this dataset, but close it and interpret it cautiously: it does not establish a homogeneous global PTEN effect, is not causal evidence, and is less central than the already validated broader clean-stratum PTEN claim H97. The current supported dataset pattern remains: SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high are strongly associated with stronger composite dependency; TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss are associated with weaker composite dependency; PTEN loss shows stronger-dependency associations in several clean conditional contexts, especially SMARCA4/TP53/KEAP1-intact contexts and the validated MSI-nonhigh clean stratum, but global PTEN remains unresolved because both discovery and validation lower bounds do not clear the threshold. Interactions are mostly nonmeaningful except for the suggestive but unresolved TP53-by-KEAP1 interaction H102 (+0.210 [0.019,0.400]), which should remain active but is not yet scientifically decisive. Technical and demographic checks are reassuringly negative for large confounding gradients: broad media-serum contrasts and male versus female are below the meaningful threshold. Next I will prioritize the registered active PTEN boundary contrasts that are less nested than H104, especially H86 (PTEN in MSI-nonhigh), H96 (PTEN in adenocarcinoma excluding MSI-high), and the single central-predictor-intact PTEN contrasts H60, H62, and H64. I will also complete the MSI-high robustness map with H91-H94 and H95, finish broad marker checks H37 and H38, and evaluate H58 as a remaining media check. I will not pursue further high-multiplicity PTEN or marker mining unless these registered comparisons produce a sharper focused question.

Iteration 8/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,

and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: No discovery assessments are due. The current evidence base is now dominated by four central associations: SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high are robustly associated with stronger composite dependency, while TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss are robustly associated with weaker composite dependency. PTEN loss is the main boundary predictor: it is accepted in several clean or MSI-nonhigh contexts, including independently validated clean central-intact/MSI-nonhigh samples, but global PTEN remains unresolved because discovery and validation lower bounds do not clear the 0.15 composite-unit threshold. I am therefore registering three focused refinements around PTEN rather than broad exploratory mining. First, I refine the near-threshold PTEN comparison in MSI-nonhigh samples by restricting to cells with matched RNA/DNA and CRISPR QC. H86 gave signed estimate +0.234 with lower bound +0.138; this refinement tests whether the same association is more precise in technically/omics-available samples. Second, I refine the adenocarcinoma MSI-nonhigh PTEN comparison with the same QC eligibility. H96 had signed estimate +0.232 with lower bound +0.120; if QC-restricted estimates clear the threshold in the same direction, the PTEN-loss stronger-dependency association would look more stable in common, higher-quality, MSI-nonhigh contexts. Third, I register a PTEN-loss-by-QC-status interaction to ask whether omics/CRISPR availability modifies the PTEN-loss association. This is a falsifiable test of whether global PTEN uncertainty is at least partly technical-context dependence. Plausible outcomes are null interaction, PTEN effect larger in QC-available samples, or PTEN effect larger in the QC-limited complement. I defer H45/H46 because they largely duplicate the already tested TP53/KEAP1-by-SMARCA4 architecture, and defer H58 because the broader media contrast H105 was nonmeaningful; I activate H73 because PTEN-loss-by-lineage interaction remains important to the adenocarcinoma-specific boundary. All claims remain descriptive associations in this dataset, not causal claims, not single-gene knockout specificity for the composite endpoint, and not evidence of generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 8/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: No discovery assessments are currently due, so this stage is used to request twelve registered but previously untested comparisons that sharpen the central scientific map without unnecessary multiplicity mining. The first priority is PTEN-loss, the main boundary predictor. H60, H62, and H64 test PTEN-loss stronger dependency when SMARCA4, TP53, or KEAP1 is intact, respectively; this asks whether the accepted PTEN signals in cleaner conditional strata persist when only one central predictor is held absent, rather than requiring the more selected triple-intact context. H73 tests whether PTEN-loss association is modified by lineage subtype, clarifying whether the adenocarcinoma-related PTEN signals are subtype-dependent. The second priority is the new technical/omics refinements: H107 and H108 replicate the near-threshold MSI-nonhigh and adenocarcinoma/MSI-nonhigh PTEN comparisons within cells having matched RNA/DNA and CRISPR QC, while H109 directly tests whether omics/CRISPR availability modifies the PTEN-loss association. These tests are informative for whether global PTEN uncertainty reflects biological conditionality, technical/availability context, or simply nonmeaningful effect size. The third priority is MSI-high robustness. MSI-high is already accepted and validated globally as associated with stronger dependency, but H92, H93, and H94 test whether that association remains meaningful in SMARCA4-intact, TP53-loss, and KEAP1-loss backgrounds. This completes part of the conditional map for the strongest non-SMARCA4 predictor and helps interpret whether MSI-high operates largely additively with the central genetic predictors. Finally, H37 and H38 complete the remaining broad marker screen for EGFR amplification and BRAF V600E, with the goal of closing unexamined conventional molecular annotations rather than pursuing further PTEN or MSI strata. I am deferring redundant symmetric central interactions, H45/H46, the narrower media check H58, and lower-priority refinements such as H95 and additional Cdkn2a context analyses unless these requested results produce a new focused question. All requested contrasts are interpreted as dataset-internal descriptive associations; acceptance does not imply causality, single-gene knockout specificity for the composite dependency endpoint, or external generalizability.

Iteration 8/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All estimates are interpreted as already signed to the claimed hypothesis direction and compared with the 0.15 composite-unit threshold. H62 is the key new PTEN result: PTEN loss versus intact in TP53-intact samples has signed estimate +0.2586 with interval +0.1686 to +0.3486. The full interval is above the threshold and in the PTEN-loss stronger-dependency direction, so I accept it. It is less nested than earlier accepted clean-context PTEN claims and has an adequate exposed cell, although it is still a conditional stratum and PTEN has been repeatedly tested, so I keep it active and request independent validation. H60 and H64 are near-threshold PTEN contrasts in SMARCA4-intact and KEAP1-intact samples, respectively: +0.2383 lower +0.1396 and +0.2325 lower +0.1327. Their point estimates are meaningful and consistent with accepted PTEN conditional patterns, but their lower bounds remain below the practical threshold. I therefore leave them unresolved but active because they are central PTEN boundary contexts; I do not accept them. The QC-restricted PTEN refinements H107 and H108 did not improve precision enough: +0.2451 lower +0.1395 and +0.2372 lower +0.1150. Because they are refinements of already unresolved MSI-nonhigh and adenocarcinoma/MSI-nonhigh PTEN contrasts and do not clear the threshold, I defer them. H109 tests whether PTEN-loss association is modified by matched omics/CRISPR QC availability; it is small and wide, +0.0792 [-0.1744, 0.3328], so the dataset does not support the registered interaction, and I reject it. H73 tests PTEN-loss by lineage interaction and gives -0.0686 [-0.2927, 0.1555]; this is not meaningful in the claimed direction and is essentially null, so I reject it. Together, H107-H109 and H73 suggest that the accepted PTEN signals are not explained by technical/omics availability or lineage-subtype effect modification, although that conclusion is bounded by the conservative interval widths in several QC and lineage-complement cells. record.narrative: All estimates below are interpreted as already signed to the claimed hypothesis direction, with the 0.15 composite-unit threshold as the practical meaningful-effect boundary. H97 is now decisively supported at its validation deadline. PTEN loss versus intact in the clean context of SMARCA4-intact, TP53-intact, KEAP1-intact, and MSI-nonhigh samples had discovery estimate +0.260 [0.182,0.338] and independent validation +0.291 [0.168,0.414]. Both intervals are entirely above the threshold and in the PTEN-loss stronger-dependency direction, so I accept and close H97. This is the best-supported PTEN-loss association, but it is still a highly selected conditional dataset-internal association, not a global PTEN claim or causal claim. H2 closes cleanly: research_marker_e_positive versus negative gave discovery +0.021 [-0.039,0.080] and validation +0.035 [-0.052,0.121], both far below the meaningful threshold and inconsistent, so the constructed marker is not supported as meaningfully associated with composite dependency. H62 is the key new PTEN validation. PTEN loss versus intact among TP53-intact samples had discovery +0.259 [0.169,0.349], clearing the threshold, and independent validation +0.255 [0.099,0.411]. The validation point estimate is essentially unchanged and the direction is consistent, but the very conservative validation interval lower bound falls below 0.15. I therefore maintain acceptance as a discovery-supported conditional association in this dataset, but close it with the caveat that validation supports rather than strictly confirms the threshold by the independent interval. This is a relatively common and less nested PTEN context than H97 or H104, so it strengthens the conditional PTEN map: PTEN-loss stronger dependency is most evident when TP53 is intact and/or in clean central-intact contexts, while global PTEN remains uncertain. H61 changes from reject to unresolved because the new validation is not negligible but remains inconclusive. PTEN loss among SMARCA4-loss cells had discovery +0.132 [-0.060,0.323], below threshold, while validation was +0.426 [0.121,0.731]. The validation point is large, but the exposed cell is small, the interval is wide, and the lower bound remains below the threshold. I do not accept it, but the new result makes rejection too strong; I defer it rather than continue PTEN subgroup mining. The current supported dataset-internal map is therefore: SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high are robustly associated with stronger composite dependency, with independent validation; TP53 loss is robustly associated with weaker composite dependency, with independent validation; KEAP1 loss is very strongly associated with weaker composite dependency in discovery but was not independently validated globally. PTEN loss shows scientifically meaningful stronger-dependency associations in selected conditional contexts, especially TP53-intact samples and clean MSI-nonhigh contexts, but global PTEN remains unresolved because discovery and validation lower bounds do not consistently clear the threshold. Negative or nonmeaningful findings include the constructed research markers and signature interactions, most conventional markers after EGFR/BRAF checks, culture-serum contrasts, sex, and most interactions, leaving a largely additive central association map except for the suggestive but unresolved TP53-by-KEAP1 interaction H102. Remaining unresolved uncertainty is concentrated in global PTEN, several near-threshold PTEN single-predictor contexts, the SMARCA4-loss PTEN subgroup after inconsistent validation, and a few MSI-high robustness/interaction claims. The most informative next analysis is the newly registered PTEN-loss comparison restricted to TP53-intact and MSI-nonhigh samples. This combines the strongest accepted PTEN context, TP53-intact, with an MSI-nonhigh restriction that avoids the dominant MSI-high signal and provides a cleaner, broader conditional test than H97. If this clears the threshold, PTEN-loss stronger dependency becomes more stable in a less selected common context; if not, PTEN should be interpreted as conditional rather than broadly homogeneous.

H96 had signed estimate +0.232 with lower bound +0.120; if QC-restricted estimates clear the threshold in the same direction, the PTEN-loss stronger-dependency association would look more stable in common, higher-quality, MSI-nonhigh contexts. Third, I register a PTEN-loss-by-QC-status interaction to ask whether omics/CRISPR availability modifies the PTEN-loss association. This is a falsifiable test of whether global PTEN uncertainty is at least partly technical-context dependence. Plausible outcomes are null interaction, PTEN effect larger in QC-available samples, or PTEN effect larger in the QC-limited complement. The full interval is above the threshold and in the PTEN-loss stronger-dependency direction, so I accept it. It is less nested than earlier accepted clean-context PTEN claims and has an adequate exposed cell, although it is still a conditional stratum and PTEN has been repeatedly tested, so I keep it active and request independent validation. H60 and H64 are near-threshold PTEN contrasts in SMARCA4-intact and KEAP1-intact samples, respectively: +0.2383 lower +0.1396 and +0.2325 lower +0.1327. Their point estimates are meaningful and consistent with accepted PTEN conditional patterns, but their lower bounds remain below the practical threshold. I therefore leave them unresolved but active because they are central PTEN boundary contexts; I do not accept them. The QC-restricted PTEN refinements H107 and H108 did not improve precision enough: +0.2451 lower +0.1395 and +0.2372 lower +0.1150. Because they are refinements of already unresolved MSI-nonhigh and adenocarcinoma/MSI-nonhigh PTEN contrasts and do not clear the threshold, I defer them. H109 tests whether PTEN-loss association is modified by matched omics/CRISPR QC availability; it is small and wide, +0.0792 [-0.1744, 0.3328], so the dataset does not support the registered interaction, and I reject it. H73 tests PTEN-loss by lineage interaction and gives -0.0686 [-0.2927, 0.1555]; this is not meaningful in the claimed direction and is essentially null, so I reject it. Together, H107-H109 and H73 suggest that the accepted PTEN signals are not explained by technical/omics availability or lineage-subtype effect modification, although that conclusion is bounded by the conservative interval widths in several QC and lineage-complement cells. The MSI-high robustness results are decisive: MSI-high versus non-MSI-high in SMARCA4-intact samples is +0.8169 [0.6930, 0.9408], in TP53-loss samples +0.8841 [0.4552, 1.3130], and in KEAP1-loss samples +0.8542 [0.6276, 1.0808]. All full intervals are above the threshold, so I accept and close these subgroup associations, while noting the small exposed cell counts in H93 and H94. This strengthens the conclusion that MSI-high is robustly associated with stronger composite dependency and is not confined to a single central-predictor background. The remaining broad marker checks are nonmeaningful: EGFR amplification +0.0919 [-0.0137, 0.1974] and BRAF V600E -0.0488 [-0.1691, 0.0714]. I reject and close both, completing this marker screen. Overall, the dataset-internal map remains: SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high are robustly associated with stronger dependency; TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss are associated with weaker dependency; PTEN loss is conditionally associated with stronger dependency, now including the broader TP53-intact context, but global PTEN remains unresolved and the pattern appears conditional rather than homogeneous. PTEN loss versus intact in the clean context of SMARCA4-intact, TP53-intact, KEAP1-intact, and MSI-nonhigh samples had discovery estimate +0.260 [0.182,0.338] and independent validation +0.291 [0.168,0.414]. Both intervals are entirely above the threshold and in the PTEN-loss stronger-dependency direction, so I accept and close H97. This is the best-supported PTEN-loss association, but it is still a highly selected conditional dataset-internal association, not a global PTEN claim or causal claim. H2 closes cleanly: research_marker_e_positive versus negative gave discovery +0.021 [-0.039,0.080] and validation +0.035 [-0.052,0.121], both far below the meaningful threshold and inconsistent, so the constructed marker is not supported as meaningfully associated with composite dependency. H62 is the key new PTEN validation. PTEN loss versus intact among TP53-intact samples had discovery +0.259 [0.169,0.349], clearing the threshold, and independent validation +0.255 [0.099,0.411]. The validation point estimate is essentially unchanged and the direction is consistent, but the very conservative validation interval lower bound falls below 0.15. I therefore maintain acceptance as a discovery-supported conditional association in this dataset, but close it with the caveat that validation supports rather than strictly confirms the threshold by the independent interval. This is a relatively common and less nested PTEN context than H97 or H104, so it strengthens the conditional PTEN map: PTEN-loss stronger dependency is most evident when TP53 is intact and/or in clean central-intact contexts, while global PTEN remains uncertain. H61 changes from reject to unresolved because the new validation is not negligible but remains inconclusive. PTEN loss among SMARCA4-loss cells had discovery +0.132 [-0.060,0.323], below threshold, while validation was +0.426 [0.121,0.731]. The validation point is large, but the exposed cell is small, the interval is wide, and the lower bound remains below the threshold. I do not accept it, but the new result makes rejection too strong; I defer it rather than continue PTEN subgroup mining. The current supported dataset-internal map is therefore: SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high are robustly associated with stronger composite dependency, with independent validation; TP53 loss is robustly associated with weaker composite dependency, with independent validation; KEAP1 loss is very strongly associated with weaker composite dependency in discovery but was not independently validated globally. PTEN loss shows scientifically meaningful stronger-dependency associations in selected conditional contexts, especially TP53-intact samples and clean MSI-nonhigh contexts, but global PTEN remains unresolved because discovery and validation lower bounds do not consistently clear the threshold. Negative or nonmeaningful findings include the constructed research markers and signature interactions, most conventional markers after EGFR/BRAF checks, culture-serum contrasts, sex, and most interactions, leaving a largely additive central association map except for the suggestive but unresolved TP53-by-KEAP1 interaction H102. Remaining unresolved uncertainty is concentrated in global PTEN, several near-threshold PTEN single-predictor contexts, the SMARCA4-loss PTEN subgroup after inconsistent validation, and a few MSI-high robustness/interaction claims. The most informative next analysis is the newly registered PTEN-loss comparison restricted to TP53-intact and MSI-nonhigh samples. This combines the strongest accepted PTEN context, TP53-intact, with an MSI-nonhigh restriction that avoids the dominant MSI-high signal and provides a cleaner, broader conditional test than H97. If this clears the threshold, PTEN-loss stronger dependency becomes more stable in a less selected common context; if not, PTEN should be interpreted as conditional rather than broadly homogeneous."}}

record.narrative: No discovery assessments are due at this stage. The current dataset-internal map is fairly mature: SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high are robustly associated with stronger composite dependency, TP53 loss is robustly associated with weaker composite dependency, KEAP1 loss is strongly associated with weaker composite dependency in discovery, and PTEN loss shows conditional stronger-dependency signals mainly in TP53-intact or clean MSI-nonhigh contexts but remains unresolved globally. Rather than continuing broad PTEN subgroup mining, I am registering a focused set of comparisons that test the remaining important boundaries: interaction architecture among the strongest predictors, lineage context after removing the dominant MSI signal, and robustness in genomic-instability contexts. First, I refine the suggestive TP53-by-KEAP1 interaction by restricting to MSI-nonhigh samples. Existing evidence suggested TP53-loss may have a larger weaker-dependency effect when KEAP1 is lost, but the interaction could be influenced by small or MSI-confounded cells. This is a falsifiable test of nonadditive TP53-KEAP1 biology independent of MSI status. Second, I refine the SMARCA4-by-lineage interaction by restricting to MSI-nonhigh samples. The prior result suggested the SMARCA4-loss association may be stronger outside adenocarcinoma relative to adenocarcinoma; the MSI-restricted refinement tests whether that apparent subtype modification persists when the very strong MSI-high effect is removed. Third, I register an MSI-high-by-TP53-loss interaction to test whether MSI-high dependency association is additive or synergistically/attenuated by TP53 status. Existing subgroup estimates are directionally consistent with slightly stronger MSI association in TP53-loss, but that may be noise from small exposed cells. Fourth through sixth, I test whether the three strongest central associations remain meaningful in top-quartile aneuploidy_score cells excluding MSI-high. These contexts are scientifically useful because high chromosomal instability can modify fitness effects of driver losses; the alternative is that the associations are independent of CNA context and robust to genomic instability. Seventh, as a secondary exploratory robustness check, I test SMARCA4-loss association in high non-MSI mutation burden. This tests whether high mutation burden without MSI alters the strongest known dependency predictor. Directions follow the known raw signs: SMARCA4 and MSI-high raw contrasts are expected negative for stronger dependency; TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss raw contrasts are expected positive for weaker dependency. For interactions, the signed claim directions match the proposed hypotheses: TP53-by-KEAP1 direction +1 tests a positive raw interaction with TP53-loss having a larger weaker-dependency effect when KEAP1 is lost; SMARCA4-by-adenocarcinoma direction +1 tests a positive raw interaction meaning adenocarcinoma SMARCA4 effects are less negative than non-adenocarcinoma effects, i.e., stronger dependency association outside adenocarcinoma; MSI-by-TP53-loss direction -1 tests whether MSI-high effects are more negative, or stronger dependency, in TP53-loss than TP53-intact samples. All returned estimates will be interpreted as already signed to these claim directions and compared with the 0.15 composite-unit threshold. These remain descriptive dataset-internal associations, not causal claims, not single-gene knockout specificity for the composite endpoint, and not evidence of generalizability.

Conclusions remain dataset-internal descriptive associations, noncausal, non-generalizable.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No discovery assessments are due at this stage. The current dataset-internal map is fairly mature: SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high are robustly associated with stronger composite dependency, TP53 loss is robustly associated with weaker composite dependency, KEAP1 loss is strongly associated with weaker composite dependency in discovery, and PTEN loss shows conditional stronger-dependency signals mainly in TP53-intact or clean MSI-nonhigh contexts but remains unresolved globally. Rather than continuing broad PTEN subgroup mining, I am registering a focused set of comparisons that test the remaining important boundaries: interaction architecture among the strongest predictors, lineage context after removing the dominant MSI signal, and robustness in genomic-instability contexts. First, I refine the suggestive TP53-by-KEAP1 interaction by restricting to MSI-nonhigh samples. Existing evidence suggested TP53-loss may have a larger weaker-dependency effect when KEAP1 is lost, but the interaction could be influenced by small or MSI-confounded cells. This is a falsifiable test of nonadditive TP53-KEAP1 biology independent of MSI status. Second, I refine the SMARCA4-by-lineage interaction by restricting to MSI-nonhigh samples. The prior result suggested the SMARCA4-loss association may be stronger outside adenocarcinoma relative to adenocarcinoma; the MSI-restricted refinement tests whether that apparent subtype modification persists when the very strong MSI-high effect is removed. Third, I register an MSI-high-by-TP53-loss interaction to test whether MSI-high dependency association is additive or synergistically/attenuated by TP53 status. Existing subgroup estimates are directionally consistent with slightly stronger MSI association in TP53-loss, but that may be noise from small exposed cells. Fourth through sixth, I test whether the three strongest central associations remain meaningful in top-quartile aneuploidy_score cells excluding MSI-high. These contexts are scientifically useful because high chromosomal instability can modify fitness effects of driver losses; the alternative is that the associations are independent of CNA context and robust to genomic instability. Seventh, as a secondary exploratory robustness check, I test SMARCA4-loss association in high non-MSI mutation burden. This tests whether high mutation burden without MSI alters the strongest known dependency predictor. Directions follow the known raw signs: SMARCA4 and MSI-high raw contrasts are expected negative for stronger dependency; TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss raw contrasts are expected positive for weaker dependency. For interactions, the signed claim directions match the proposed hypotheses: TP53-by-KEAP1 direction +1 tests a positive raw interaction with TP53-loss having a larger weaker-dependency effect when KEAP1 is lost; SMARCA4-by-adenocarcinoma direction +1 tests a positive raw interaction meaning adenocarcinoma SMARCA4 effects are less negative than non-adenocarcinoma effects, i.e., stronger dependency association outside adenocarcinoma; MSI-by-TP53-loss direction -1 tests whether MSI-high effects are more negative, or stronger dependency, in TP53-loss than TP53-intact samples. All returned estimates will be interpreted as already signed to these claim directions and compared with the 0.15 composite-unit threshold. These remain descriptive dataset-internal associations, not causal claims, not single-gene knockout specificity for the composite endpoint, and not evidence of generalizability.","analyze":"No discovery assessments are currently due, so this stage is used to request twelve registered but previously untested comparisons that sharpen the central scientific map without unnecessary multiplicity mining. H60, H62, and H64 test PTEN-loss stronger dependency when SMARCA4, TP53, or KEAP1 is intact, respectively; this asks whether the accepted PTEN signals in cleaner conditional strata persist when only one central predictor is held absent, rather than requiring the more selected triple-intact context. H73 tests whether PTEN-loss association is modified by lineage subtype, clarifying whether the adenocarcinoma-related PTEN signals are subtype-dependent. The second priority is the new technical/omics refinements: H107 and H108 replicate the near-threshold MSI-nonhigh and adenocarcinoma/MSI-nonhigh PTEN comparisons within cells having matched RNA/DNA and CRISPR QC, while H109 directly tests whether omics/CRISPR availability modifies the PTEN-loss association. These tests are informative for whether global PTEN uncertainty reflects biological conditionality, technical/availability context, or simply nonmeaningful effect size. The third priority is MSI-high robustness. MSI-high is already accepted and validated globally as associated with stronger dependency, but H92, H93, and H94 test whether that association remains meaningful in SMARCA4-intact, TP53-loss, and KEAP1-loss backgrounds. This completes part of the conditional map for the strongest non-SMARCA4 predictor and helps interpret whether MSI-high operates largely additively with the central genetic predictors. Finally, H37 and H38 complete the remaining broad marker screen for EGFR amplification and BRAF V600E, with the goal of closing unexamined conventional molecular annotations rather than pursuing further PTEN or MSI strata. I am deferring redundant symmetric central interactions, H45/H46, the narrower media check H58, and lower-priority refinements such as H95 and additional Cdkn2a context analyses unless these requested results produce a new focused question. All requested contrasts are interpreted as dataset-internal descriptive associations; acceptance does not imply causality, single-gene knockout specificity for the composite dependency endpoint, or external generalizability.","appraise":"All estimates are interpreted as already signed to the claimed hypothesis direction and compared with the 0.15 composite-unit threshold. H62 is the key new PTEN result: PTEN loss versus intact in TP53-intact samples has signed estimate +0.2586 with interval +0.1686 to +0.3486. The full interval is above the threshold and in the PTEN-loss stronger-dependency direction, so I accept it. It is less nested than earlier accepted clean-context PTEN claims and has an adequate exposed cell, although it is still a conditional stratum and PTEN has been repeatedly tested, so I keep it active and request independent validation. H60 and H64 are near-threshold PTEN contrasts in SMARCA4-intact and KEAP1-intact samples, respectively: +0.2383 lower +0.1396 and +0.2325 lower +0.1327. Their point estimates are meaningful and consistent with accepted PTEN conditional patterns, but their lower bounds remain below the practical threshold. I therefore leave them unresolved but active because they are central PTEN boundary contexts; I do not accept them. The QC-restricted PTEN refinements H107 and H108 did not improve precision enough: +0.2451 lower +0.1395 and +0.2372 lower +0.1150. Because they are refinements of already unresolved MSI-nonhigh and adenocarcinoma/MSI-nonhigh PTEN contrasts and do not clear the threshold, I defer them. H109 tests whether PTEN-loss association is modified by matched omics/CRISPR QC availability; it is small and wide, +0.0792 [-0.1744, 0.3328], so the dataset does not support the registered interaction, and I reject it. H73 tests PTEN-loss by lineage interaction and gives -0.0686 [-0.2927, 0.1555]; this is not meaningful in the claimed direction and is essentially null, so I reject it. This is the most informative next PTEN test because it combines the strongest accepted PTEN context, TP53-intact, with an MSI-nonhigh restriction that avoids the very strong MSI-high signal, and it is less selected than the already validated clean central-intact/MSI-nonhigh PTEN context. I am also requesting H111, H112, and H113 to test interaction architecture among the central predictors: TP53-by-KEAP1 restricted to MSI-nonhigh samples, SMARCA4-by-lineage restricted to MSI-nonhigh samples, and MSI-high-by-TP53-loss. These directly test whether earlier suggestive interaction patterns survive after removing the dominant MSI signal or whether the central associations are essentially additive. H91 and H95 complete the MSI-high conditional/interaction map: H91 asks whether MSI-high remains associated with stronger dependency specifically within SMARCA4-loss cells, and H95 tests whether lineage subtype modifies the MSI-high association. Finally, H114 through H117 test robustness of the strongest predictor effects in genomic-instability contexts excluding MSI-high: SMARCA4, TP53, and KEAP1 effects in high aneuploidy_score samples, and SMARCA4 effect in high mutation_burden samples.
