Iteration 9/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All estimates are interpreted as already signed to the claimed hypothesis direction and judged against the 0.15 composite-dependency-unit threshold. H110 is the most important new result: PTEN loss versus intact among TP53-intact and MSI-nonhigh samples has signed estimate +0.2817 with interval +0.1899 to +0.3735 and adequate cells (199 exposed, 1289 comparator). The entire interval is above the threshold in the PTEN-loss stronger-dependency direction, so I accept it. This is a broader but still conditional PTEN context, less nested than already accepted and validated clean central-intact contexts such as H97, and it directly tests the main uncertainty around PTEN after earlier TP53-intact evidence. I keep it active and request independent validation because validation is the best way to assess whether this common TP53-intact/MSI-nonhigh PTEN association is robust within this dataset. H114 through H117 also support robustness of the central predictors outside MSI-high. SMARCA4 loss remains strongly associated with stronger dependency in high aneuploidy_score samples excluding MSI-high (+0.7960 [0.6481, 0.9439]) and in high mutation_burden samples excluding MSI-high (+0.7283 [0.5587, 0.8979]). TP53 loss remains associated with weaker dependency in high aneuploidy_score samples excluding MSI-high (+0.4616 [0.2703, 0.6529]), and KEAP1 loss remains associated with weaker dependency in the same context (+0.8639 [0.7259, 1.0019]). All four full intervals clear the threshold in the registered directions, so I accept and close them as dataset-internal robustness evidence. H91 shows MSI-high remains associated with stronger dependency within SMARCA4-loss cells (+0.6355 [0.4479, 0.8231]), with a full interval above threshold, so I accept and close it, noting the exposed cell is small (29) and the interval is somewhat wide. This is consistent with MSI-high being robust across central predictor backgrounds. The interaction architecture remains largely unsupported at the threshold level. H111 tests TP53-loss by KEAP1-loss interaction restricted to MSI-nonhigh samples; the signed estimate is +0.1382 with interval -0.0565 to +0.3329. The point is below threshold and the interval includes zero, so I reject this registered interaction. This weakens the earlier suggestive H102 TP53-by-KEAP1 interaction, and I move H102 from active to deferred because the MSI-restricted refinement did not clear the threshold. H112 tests SMARCA4-loss by lineage interaction restricted to MSI-nonhigh samples; the signed estimate is +0.2146 with interval +0.0656 to +0.3636. The point exceeds threshold, but the lower bound remains below threshold, and this resembles the earlier unrefined H78 result. I therefore leave H112 unresolved and defer further investigation; I also defer H78 because H112 does not resolve the interaction. H113 tests MSI-high by TP53-loss interaction; the signed estimate is +0.1235 with wide interval -0.3163 to +0.5633. The exposed MSI-high/TP53-loss cell is small (24), and the result is below threshold and imprecise, so I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than closing as a precise null. H95 tests MSI-high by lineage subtype interaction; the signed estimate is -0.1760 with interval -0.4351 to +0.0831. It is not consistently meaningful in the claimed direction and includes zero, so I reject and close it. Overall, the dataset-internal map strengthens: SMARCA4 loss, MSI-high, TP53 loss, and KEAP1 loss effects are robust across genomic-instability contexts; MSI-high remains associated with stronger dependency even within SMARCA4-loss cells; PTEN loss now has a new accepted TP53-intact/MSI-nonhigh conditional association pending independent validation. Interaction evidence remains weak, with only H110 receiving validation because it most directly clarifies the remaining PTEN boundary. All conclusions are descriptive and dataset-internal, not causal, not single-gene knockout specificity for the composite endpoint, and not evidence of external generalizability.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

record.narrative: All estimates are already signed to the claimed hypothesis direction, and the practical threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units. H104 is assessed at its validation deadline. PTEN loss versus intact in the highly selected clean context of adenocarcinoma, MSI-nonhigh, SMARCA4-intact, TP53-intact, and KEAP1-intact cells had discovery estimate +0.279 [0.186, 0.373] and independent validation +0.203 [0.073, 0.333]. The validation point estimate is in the same PTEN-loss stronger-dependency direction and has meaningful magnitude, but the very conservative validation lower bound does not clear the threshold. I therefore maintain acceptance as a discovery-supported conditional association in this dataset and close it, with the caveat that validation supports rather than independently confirms the threshold in that selected context. H110 is the key new PTEN result. PTEN loss versus intact among TP53-intact and MSI-nonhigh samples had discovery +0.282 [0.190, 0.374] and independent validation +0.275 [0.143, 0.406]. The discovery evidence fully cleared the threshold, and validation is highly consistent in point estimate and direction. The validation lower bound is only slightly below 0.15, so independent confirmation of the threshold is not strict, but the result strongly supports PTEN-loss stronger dependency in this broader, less nested TP53-intact/MSI-nonhigh context. I accept and close H110. Together with H62, H66, H68, H80, H97, and H104, the PTEN map remains conditional: PTEN-loss stronger dependency is most evident when TP53 is intact and/or in MSI-nonhigh and clean central-intact backgrounds, while global PTEN remains unresolved. I mark near-threshold PTEN single-context claims H60, H64, H86, and H96 deferred rather than continuing to mine similar near-boundary contexts without new information. The current supported dataset-internal map is: SMARCA4 loss is robustly associated with stronger composite dependency, with independent validation and robustness in high aneuploidy and high non-MSI mutation-burden contexts; MSI-high is robustly associated with stronger composite dependency, with independent validation and persistence across SMARCA4-loss/intact, TP53-loss, KEAP1-loss, lineage, and clean contexts; TP53 loss is robustly associated with weaker composite dependency, with independent validation and robustness in high-aneuploidy non-MSI contexts; KEAP1 loss is very strongly associated with weaker composite dependency in discovery and many subgroup contexts, but global independent validation remains pending. I leave H14 active because it is the highest-priority remaining central validation target. Negative or nonmeaningful findings include all constructed research markers and their signature interactions, most conventional driver or marker associations after the EGFR/BRAF screen, STK11, MTAP, BRCA2, RB1, NF1, SMAD4, APC, ERBB2, PIK3CA, MYC amplification, sex, media-serum contrasts, CRISPR-library or matched-omics availability effects, and most effect-modifier interactions. The central association map remains largely additive, with unresolved or rejected interactions including TP53-by-SMARCA4, KEAP1-by-SMARCA4, PTEN-by-SMARCA4/TP53/KEAP1/lineage/QC, MSI-by-lineage, MSI-by-TP53, SMARCA4-by-lineage, and TP53-by-KEAP1 variants. Unresolved scientific uncertainty is concentrated in global PTEN, several near-threshold PTEN contexts, PTEN within SMARCA4-loss after inconsistent validation, and a few interactions or central robustness checks. The most informative next analysis is independent validation of H14 global KEAP1 loss. The newly registered robustness comparisons are also useful: PTEN loss in TP53-intact, MSI-nonhigh, high-aneuploidy samples tests whether the accepted PTEN context survives chromosomal instability, while KEAP1 and TP53 loss in high non-MSI mutation burden complete central robustness in genomic-instability backgrounds. The validation lower bound is only slightly below 0.15, so independent confirmation of the threshold is not strict, but the result strongly supports PTEN-loss stronger dependency in this broader, less nested TP53-intact/MSI-nonhigh context. I accept and close H110. Together with H62, H66, H68, H80, H97, and H104, the PTEN map remains conditional: PTEN-loss stronger dependency is most evident when TP53 is intact and/or in MSI-nonhigh and clean central-intact backgrounds, while global PTEN remains unresolved. I mark near-threshold PTEN single-context claims H60, H64, H86, and H96 deferred rather than continuing to mine similar near-boundary contexts without new information. The current supported dataset-internal map is: SMARCA4 loss is robustly associated with stronger composite dependency, with independent validation and robustness in high aneuploidy and high non-MSI mutation-burden contexts; MSI-high is robustly associated with stronger composite dependency, with independent validation and persistence across SMARCA4-loss/intact, TP53-loss, KEAP1-loss, lineage, and clean contexts; TP53 loss is robustly associated with weaker composite dependency, with independent validation and robustness in high-aneuploidy non-MSI contexts; KEAP1 loss is very strongly associated with weaker composite dependency in discovery and many subgroup contexts, but global independent validation remains pending. I leave H14 active because it is the highest-priority remaining central validation target. Negative or nonmeaningful findings include all constructed research markers and their signature interactions, most conventional driver or marker associations after the EGFR/BRAF screen, STK11, MTAP, BRCA2, RB1, NF1, SMAD4, APC, ERBB2, PIK3CA, MYC amplification, sex, media-serum contrasts, CRISPR-library or matched-omics availability effects, and most effect-modifier interactions. Unresolved scientific uncertainty is concentrated in global PTEN, several near-threshold PTEN contexts, PTEN within SMARCA4-loss after inconsistent validation, and a few interactions or central robustness checks. The most informative next analysis is independent validation of H14 global KEAP1 loss. The newly registered robustness comparisons are also useful: PTEN loss in TP53-intact, MSI-nonhigh, high-aneuploidy samples tests whether the accepted PTEN context survives chromosomal instability, while KEAP1 and TP53 loss in high non-MSI mutation burden complete central robustness in genomic-instability backgrounds. record.narrative: No discovery assessments are currently due. The current dataset-internal map is mature: SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high are robustly associated with stronger composite dependency, TP53 loss is robustly associated with weaker composite dependency, and KEAP1 loss is strongly associated with weaker composite dependency, especially in many conditional contexts. PTEN loss is best supported as a conditional stronger-dependency predictor in TP53-intact and MSI-nonhigh backgrounds, while global PTEN remains unresolved. The newly active comparisons H118, H119, and H120 already test PTEN in TP53-intact/MSI-nonhigh/high aneuploidy and TP53/KEAP1 in high non-MSI mutation burden. I am therefore registering three focused refinements that address remaining boundaries without repeating already tested near-threshold PTEN contexts. First, PTEN loss in TP53-intact, MSI-nonhigh, high mutation_burden samples tests whether the accepted TP53-intact/MSI-nonhigh PTEN association remains meaningful under elevated mutational burden without MSI. The alternative is that PTEN effects are more tightly linked to the broader TP53-intact/MSI-nonhigh state and attenuate once non-MSI mutational load is high. Second, MSI-high in high mutation_burden samples tests whether the very strong MSI-high association persists after conditioning on mutation burden. If MSI-high remains strongly associated with stronger dependency in high mutation burden, that supports an MSI-specific association beyond simple mutation-burden correlation; if it attenuates below the 0.15-unit threshold, mutation burden or correlated MSI-high biology may explain more of the original association. Third, SMARCA4 loss in high ploidy and MSI-nonhigh samples tests the strongest known predictor under an alternative chromosomal-instability measure distinct from aneuploidy_score. This is a robustness test: if SMARCA4-loss stronger dependency persists with elevated ploidy, the association is less likely to be an artifact of the specific aneuploidy metric. Directions follow the known raw contrasts: SMARCA4-loss and MSI-high raw contrasts are expected negative, so claims with direction -1 are signed positive if stronger dependency is observed; PTEN-loss in accepted conditional contexts also has negative raw contrast, so direction -1 tests stronger dependency with PTEN loss. All proposed estimates will be interpreted as already signed to the registered direction and judged against the 0.15 composite dependency-score threshold. These remain descriptive, dataset-internal associations, not causal effects, not single-gene knockout specificity for the composite endpoint, and not evidence of external generalizability. If H121 and H122 clear threshold, PTEN becomes more robust in a genomic-instability/nonMSI background and MSI remains specific after mutation-burden conditioning. If they do not, PTEN and MSI should remain interpreted as conditional or context-limited within this dataset. H123, if clear, further strengthens SMARCA4-loss robustness across chromosomal-instability contexts; if not, SMARCA4 may be somewhat sensitive to ploidy context. For remaining validation priority, global KEAP1 loss remains the most useful active target because it is the only central predictor without independent validation.

prompt:
Iteration 10/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: No discovery assessments are due, so this analyze stage requests all currently active untested comparisons rather than rerunning already tested claims, because tested claims would reuse the same data and provide no new sample. The selected six claims sharpen the remaining central and PTEN boundaries. H118 tests whether the accepted PTEN-loss stronger-dependency association survives when TP53-intact and MSI-nonhigh samples additionally have high aneuploidy_score, a genomic-instability stress that could attenuate PTEN effects. H121 tests whether PTEN-loss stronger dependency remains meaningful in TP53-intact, MSI-nonhigh samples with high mutation_burden, distinguishing a broad TP53-intact/MSI-nonhigh PTEN effect from attenuation under nonMSI mutational burden. H122 tests whether MSI-high remains associated with stronger dependency after conditioning on high mutation_burden, which is important because MSI-high is strongly associated with mutation burden; persistence would support an MSI-specific association beyond simple mutational-load correlation. H119 and H120 complete central robustness by asking whether KEAP1-loss and TP53-loss associations remain meaningful in high nonMSI mutation_burden, complementing the already tested high-aneuploidy nonMSI robustness results for KEAP1 and TP53. H123 tests SMARCA4-loss stronger dependency in high ploidy, MSI-nonhigh samples, providing robustness under an alternative chromosomal-instability measure distinct from aneuploidy_score. These six analyses are more informative than rerunning H14, H58, near-threshold PTEN contexts, or deferred central interactions because they test new contexts and may materially change the dataset-internal interpretation of PTEN, MSI, and SMARCA4. All returned estimates will already be signed to the registered hypothesis direction and judged against the 0.15 composite-dependency-unit threshold. Conclusions remain descriptive, dataset-internal associations, not causal effects, not single-gene knockout specificity for the composite endpoint, and not evidence of external generalizability. H14 global KEAP1 loss remains active and should be considered for the next voluntary validation request if no more urgent validation need emerges from these results.

Iteration 10/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.

PTEN loss is best supported as a conditional stronger-dependency predictor in TP53-intact and MSI-nonhigh backgrounds, while global PTEN remains unresolved. The newly active comparisons H118, H119, and H120 already test PTEN in TP53-intact/MSI-nonhigh/high aneuploidy and TP53/KEAP1 in high non-MSI mutation burden. I am therefore registering three focused refinements that address remaining boundaries without repeating already tested near-threshold PTEN contexts. First, PTEN loss in TP53-intact, MSI-nonhigh, high mutation_burden samples tests whether the accepted TP53-intact/MSI-nonhigh PTEN association remains meaningful under elevated mutational burden without MSI. The alternative is that PTEN effects are more tightly linked to the broader TP53-intact/MSI-nonhigh state and attenuate once non-MSI mutational load is high. Second, MSI-high in high mutation_burden samples tests whether the very strong MSI-high association persists after conditioning on mutation burden. If MSI-high remains strongly associated with stronger dependency in high mutation burden, that supports an MSI-specific association beyond simple mutation-burden correlation; if it attenuates below the 0.15-unit threshold, mutation burden or correlated MSI-high biology may explain more of the original association. Third, SMARCA4 loss in high ploidy and MSI-nonhigh samples tests the strongest known predictor under an alternative chromosomal-instability measure distinct from aneuploidy_score. This is a robustness test: if SMARCA4-loss stronger dependency persists with elevated ploidy, the association is less likely to be an artifact of the specific aneuploidy metric. Directions follow the known raw contrasts: SMARCA4-loss and MSI-high raw contrasts are expected negative, so claims with direction -1 are signed positive if stronger dependency is observed; PTEN-loss in accepted conditional contexts also has negative raw contrast, so direction -1 tests stronger dependency with PTEN loss. All proposed estimates will be interpreted as already signed to the registered direction and judged against the 0.15 composite dependency-score threshold. These remain descriptive, dataset-internal associations, not causal effects, not single-gene knockout specificity for the composite endpoint, and not evidence of external generalizability. H110 is the most important new result: PTEN loss versus intact among TP53-intact and MSI-nonhigh samples has signed estimate +0.2817 with interval +0.1899 to +0.3735 and adequate cells (199 exposed, 1289 comparator). The entire interval is above the threshold in the PTEN-loss stronger-dependency direction, so I accept it. This is a broader but still conditional PTEN context, less nested than already accepted and validated clean central-intact contexts such as H97, and it directly tests the main uncertainty around PTEN after earlier TP53-intact evidence. I keep it active and request independent validation because validation is the best way to assess whether this common TP53-intact/MSI-nonhigh PTEN association is robust within this dataset. H114 through H117 also support robustness of the central predictors outside MSI-high. SMARCA4 loss remains strongly associated with stronger dependency in high aneuploidy_score samples excluding MSI-high (+0.7960 [0.6481, 0.9439]) and in high mutation_burden samples excluding MSI-high (+0.7283 [0.5587, 0.8979]). TP53 loss remains associated with weaker dependency in high aneuploidy_score samples excluding MSI-high (+0.4616 [0.2703, 0.6529]), and KEAP1 loss remains associated with weaker dependency in the same context (+0.8639 [0.7259, 1.0019]). All four full intervals clear the threshold in the registered directions, so I accept and close them as dataset-internal robustness evidence. H91 shows MSI-high remains associated with stronger dependency within SMARCA4-loss cells (+0.6355 [0.4479, 0.8231]), with a full interval above threshold, so I accept and close it, noting the exposed cell is small (29) and the interval is somewhat wide. This is consistent with MSI-high being robust across central predictor backgrounds. The interaction architecture remains largely unsupported at the threshold level. H111 tests TP53-loss by KEAP1-loss interaction restricted to MSI-nonhigh samples; the signed estimate is +0.1382 with interval -0.0565 to +0.3329. The point is below threshold and the interval includes zero, so I reject this registered interaction. This weakens the earlier suggestive H102 TP53-by-KEAP1 interaction, and I move H102 from active to deferred because the MSI-restricted refinement did not clear the threshold. H112 tests SMARCA4-loss by lineage interaction restricted to MSI-nonhigh samples; the signed estimate is +0.2146 with interval +0.0656 to +0.3636. The point exceeds threshold, but the lower bound remains below threshold, and this resembles the earlier unrefined H78 result. I therefore leave H112 unresolved and defer further investigation; I also defer H78 because H112 does not resolve the interaction. H113 tests MSI-high by TP53-loss interaction; the signed estimate is +0.1235 with wide interval -0.3163 to +0.5633. The exposed MSI-high/TP53-loss cell is small (24), and the result is below threshold and imprecise, so I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than closing as a precise null. H95 tests MSI-high by lineage subtype interaction; the signed estimate is -0.1760 with interval -0.4351 to +0.0831. It is not consistently meaningful in the claimed direction and includes zero, so I reject and close it. record.narrative: All new estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction and judged against 0.15 composite dependency-score units. H119, H120, H122, and H123 provide new robustness evidence for the central predictors. H119 tests KEAP1 loss in high nonMSI mutation-burden samples: signed estimate +0.759 (95% CI +0.600 to +0.918), cells 53/227; the full interval clears the threshold in the weaker-dependency direction, so I accept and close it. H120 tests TP53 loss in the same high nonMSI mutation-burden context: signed estimate +0.488 (95% CI +0.265 to +0.711), cells 58/222; the full interval clears the threshold, so TP53-loss weaker dependency is robust there and I accept and close it. H122 is scientifically important because it tests whether the strong MSI-high stronger-dependency association survives conditioning on high mutation burden: signed estimate +0.753 (95% CI +0.565 to +0.940), cells 59/280. This clears threshold comfortably and supports an MSI-specific dataset-internal association rather than one fully explained by mutational burden. H123 tests SMARCA4 loss under elevated ploidy while excluding MSI-high: signed estimate +0.943 (95% CI +0.816 to +1.070), cells 100/420; this is a strong alternative chromosomal-instability robustness result, so I accept and close it. H118 tests PTEN loss within TP53-intact, MSI-nonhigh, high-aneuploidy samples: signed estimate +0.216 (95% CI +0.041 to +0.392), cells 49/265. The point estimate is above threshold and directionally consistent with accepted PTEN-loss stronger dependency, but the lower bound is below threshold and the exposed cell is small. Given many nearby PTEN-context analyses, I do not accept this selected context; I leave it unresolved but defer it rather than continue mining near-threshold PTEN subgroups. H121 tests PTEN loss in TP53-intact, MSI-nonhigh, high-mutation-burden samples: signed estimate +0.113 (95% CI -0.106 to +0.333), cells 31/191. The point is below threshold and the interval includes zero, so I reject this specific context and close it. This suggests that the broader TP53-intact/MSI-nonhigh PTEN association, while accepted overall, attenuates or becomes undetectable when nonMSI mutational burden is high. I request validation for H14, global KEAP1 loss. It is the highest-priority central predictor lacking independent validation: discovery signed estimate +0.832 (95% CI +0.766 to +0.897), cells 393/1607, and validation would consolidate the global association before additional conditional KEAP1 analyses. Iteration 10/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units

record.narrative: All estimates below are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction and are judged against the practical threshold of 0.15 composite dependency-score units. H62 reassesses PTEN loss within TP53-intact samples. The discovery estimate was +0.259 (95% CI +0.169 to +0.349), fully above threshold in the stronger-dependency direction, and independent validation was highly consistent in direction and magnitude: +0.255, although its very conservative lower bound (+0.099) falls just below threshold. Because the discovery evidence was strong and the validation is directionally and practically supportive, I maintain acceptance of H62 and close it. H61 reassesses PTEN loss within SMARCA4-loss samples. Discovery showed only +0.132 (95% CI -0.060 to +0.323), below threshold and crossing zero, while independent validation showed +0.426 but with lower bound +0.121, again not independently confirming the threshold. With small exposed cells and inconsistent threshold evidence, I cannot accept this context, but I also do not reject it as a precise null; it remains unresolved and is closed because additional near-boundary PTEN mining would not be informative. H14 reassesses global KEAP1 loss. Discovery was +0.832 (95% CI +0.766 to +0.897), and independent validation was +0.803 (95% CI +0.702 to +0.905). Both discovery and validation clear the threshold comfortably in the KEAP1-loss weaker-dependency direction, so I accept and close H14. This completes independent validation of the four central predictors: SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high are associated with stronger composite dependency, while TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss are associated with weaker composite dependency. The supported dataset-internal map is now mature and largely additive: SMARCA4-loss and MSI-high stronger-dependency associations are robust across many contexts including high chromosomal instability and high non-MSI mutation burden; TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss weaker-dependency associations are also robust across many contexts; PTEN loss is best supported conditionally in TP53-intact and MSI-nonhigh or clean central-intact backgrounds, with global and SMARCA4-loss-specific contexts remaining uncertain or near-threshold. Negative or nonmeaningful findings include constructed research markers and their signature interactions, most conventional driver or marker associations after broad screening, most effect-modifier interactions, and technical availability/library contrasts tested to date. No further voluntary validation requests remain, and central validation priorities are complete. The most informative next analyses are focused robustness tests of the validated central predictors in untested biological-state contexts, using top-quartile EMT, stemness, 8q24 copy gain, hypoxia, and IFN-gamma score subgroups restricted to MSI-nonhigh samples. If these central effects remain threshold-clearing there, the dataset-internal association map is even less sensitive to biological-state context; if they attenuate or cross zero, those contexts should be identified as boundaries. I avoided further near-threshold PTEN subgroup mining because the available evidence is inconsistent and likely underpowered. All conclusions remain descriptive, dataset-internal associations, not causal effects, not evidence of single-gene knockout mechanism specificity for the composite endpoint, and not evidence of external generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 11/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,

record.narrative: No discovery assessments are currently due, and no further voluntary validation can be requested. The accepted central predictor map is now well supported: SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high are associated with stronger composite dependency, while TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss are associated with weaker composite dependency. The remaining useful scientific question is whether these associations remain practically meaningful in distinct biological-state and chromosomal-instability contexts. The currently active comparisons H124-H128 test SMARCA4 loss in high EMT, high stemness, or high 8q24 copy number, TP53 loss in high hypoxia, and KEAP1 loss in high IFN-gamma signature, all restricted to MSI-nonhigh samples. I now register seven complementary context-robustness comparisons. Five test MSI-high, the central predictor with strong global and many conditional supports, within top-quartile EMT, stemness, 8q24 copy gain, hypoxia, or IFN-gamma states. Because the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast for MSI-high versus MSI-nonhigh is expected to be negative, these claims use direction -1; signed positive estimates would indicate stronger dependency among MSI-high samples in the named biological context. If all remain above the 0.15 threshold, MSI-high would be robust across immune, hypoxia, de-differentiation, and proliferative-copy contexts. If any fall near or below threshold, those contexts should be reported as boundaries rather than evidence that MSI-high is a general effect. Two additional comparisons test TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss in high-ploidy MSI-nonhigh samples. These extend the accepted global associations to an alternative chromosomal-instability measure distinct from aneuploidy_score and complement the accepted high-aneuploidy and high-nonMSI-mutation-burden robustness results. TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss raw contrasts are expected to be positive, so claims use direction +1; signed positive estimates indicate weaker dependency, consistent with the accepted global map. This registration yields 12 active untested comparisons including the prior active set, allowing the next analyze stage to test the full focused robustness panel at once. All conclusions will remain descriptive and dataset-internal, not causal, not evidence of single-gene knockout specificity for the composite endpoint, and not external generalizability.

censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.

H129-H133 test the reverse central predictor MSI-high in top-quartile biological-state contexts. prompt:
Iteration 11/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All twelve delivered estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction and are compared with the 0.15 composite-dependency-unit absolute threshold. H124, H125, and H126 test SMARCA4-loss stronger dependency in MSI-nonhigh samples with high EMT, stemness, or 8q24 copy gain: signed estimates +0.821 (95% CI +0.683 to +0.958), +0.618 (+0.474 to +0.763), and +0.836 (+0.719 to +0.952), respectively. Each full interval exceeds threshold in the stronger-dependency direction, so I accept and close them. H127 and H128 test TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss weaker dependency in high-hypoxia and high IFN-gamma contexts, respectively: signed estimates +0.505 (+0.319 to +0.690) and +0.756 (+0.619 to +0.893). Both intervals clear threshold in the weaker-dependency direction, supporting robustness of these accepted central associations in those biological-state contexts. H129 through H133 test MSI-high stronger dependency in top-quartile EMT, stemness, 8q24 copy gain, hypoxia, and IFN-gamma samples: signed estimates +0.654 (+0.424 to +0.885), +0.780 (+0.548 to +1.012), +0.830 (+0.613 to +1.047), +0.840 (+0.572 to +1.109), and +0.817 (+0.649 to +0.985). Although exposed MSI-high cells are modest (28-57), all cells meet the minimum-20 rule and all intervals remain well above the practical threshold. I accept and close them, while noting they remain dataset-internal conditional associations rather than independent replication. H134 and H135 test TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss weaker dependency in high-ploidy MSI-nonhigh samples: signed estimates +0.378 (+0.176 to +0.579) and +0.913 (+0.787 to +1.038). Both clear the threshold; H134 is the least conservative because its lower bound is closer to threshold, but the point estimate is still substantially above 0.15. I accept and close both. Critical-review considerations: these twelve comparisons are simultaneous robustness probes, so multiplicity is relevant. However, the magnitude of the effects and the fact that all lower bounds exceed the effect-size threshold reduce concern that the acceptances are primarily false-positive multiplicity artifacts. The analyses use measured top-quartile biological-state variables and assumed they are non-outcome-derived and non-collinear; without further model-based adjustment or independent replication, they should be interpreted as descriptive subgroup associations, not causal effects, not single-gene-knockout mechanism specificity, and not external generalizability claims. No validation request is made because the remaining voluntary validation budget is zero and the global central predictor effects have already been independently validated; these results refine boundary conditions for already validated central associations.

Iteration 11/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every

record.narrative:
H110 is the only response-deadline assessment. It tests PTEN loss versus PTEN wild type within TP53-intact and MSI-nonhigh samples, with the hypothesis signed in the stronger-dependency direction. Discovery R108 is +0.282 (95% CI +0.190 to +0.374), entirely above the 0.15 composite-unit threshold. Independent validation R118 is +0.275 (95% CI +0.143 to +0.406); its point estimate is well above threshold and its direction is highly concordant, although the very conservative validation lower bound falls just below 0.15. I therefore maintain acceptance: discovery alone was decisive, and validation is practical and directionally supportive rather than contradictory. The claim remains a descriptive association in this dataset: PTEN loss is associated with stronger composite dependency in this TP53-intact/MSI-nonhigh background. It does not establish causality, a gene-specific mechanism, or external generalizability.

This completes the immediate PTEN follow-up map. PTEN loss is best supported conditionally in TP53-intact and MSI-nonhigh or otherwise clean central backgrounds. PTEN global effects remain near threshold and should not be overinterpreted, and the SMARCA4-loss-specific PTEN context remains uncertain. Many remaining PTEN, CDKN2A, media, lineage-interaction, and small-cell central-interaction uncertainties have near-threshold or underpowered evidence. I closed those unresolved deferred investigations because additional near-boundary mining on the same data is unlikely to be informative and could create false precision. This is a focus decision, not rejection of those hypotheses; they remain unresolved with respect to generalization.

The mature supported map is broad and dataset-internal: SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high are associated with stronger composite dependency, whereas TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss are associated with weaker composite dependency. These central associations have discovery support, several independent validations, and robustness across many technical, genomic-instability, mutation-burden, ploidy, subtype, and top-quartile biological-state contexts. Negative or nonmeaningful findings include the constructed research markers and signature interactions, most conventional driver associations, many interaction tests, serum, sex, CRISPR-library, matched omics, and apc/erbb2/pik3ca/brca2/braf/myc/egfr/kras contexts tested. 

The most informative next analyses are not additional near-threshold subgroup mining. I registered focused chromosomal-instability robustness and interaction tests: MSI-high means in top-half high ploidy and high aneuploidy to complete the central high-CIN context panel, and interaction tests of SMARCA4 loss, TP53 loss, and KEAP1 loss with high ploidy among MSI-nonhigh samples. I also registered an MSI-high x top-half-ploidy interaction. These ask whether the accepted central means are truly additive across high chromosomal instability or whether ploidy is an effect-modifying boundary. If interactions fail to clear the threshold, that supports additive context robustness; if they clear in the relevant direction, they identify a genuine boundary condition. All conclusions remain descriptive and limited to this supplied dataset.
